action.question: What role does the 'new repo' play after the history rewrite lands?

questions.question: What role does the 'new repo' play after the history rewrite lands?

options.label: New becomes the daily-driver; current FamilyFund retires
options.description: Rename current `FamilyFund` → `FamilyFund-pre-rewrite-archive` (private, frozen reference). Rename new → `FamilyFund`. Re-clone macbook + this Mac. Future PRs land on the new repo. Simplest going forward but more cleanup.

options.label: New is the sanitized source for FamilyFund-public only
options.description: Keep `FamilyFund` as daily-driver (with its dirty history); the new repo (e.g. `FamilyFund-sync`) is a periodically-rewritten mirror used solely for syncing to `FamilyFund-public`. Two-step sanitization. Less migration cost but adds a step to every sync.

options.label: Build new → mirror-push to FamilyFund-public directly, skip naming question
options.description: Worker creates scratch clone, rewrites, gitleaks-verifies clean, then `gh repo create FamilyFund-public --public` + push the rewritten history. `FamilyFund` stays dirty privately; public gets the clean rewrite. Solves the SOP block AND the first sync in one shot.

questions.question: Session-skills PR — approve the 3 default behavior changes?

options.label: Approve autogen name: oneoff-<host>-<8hex> → oneoff-<8hex>
options.description: Host segment is redundant (titles watcher already prefixes [NICK.host]). Picker rows + log filenames lose the host fragment.

options.label: Approve --reply-to defaults to AUTO from JWT
options.description: Sender id auto-detected from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ACCESS_TOKEN. Manager pattern just works; pass --no-reply-to to opt out.

options.label: Approve --subname AUTO when --wait/--prompt is set
options.description: Inner session title gets an extra [SLUG] bracket so sub-sessions are visually distinct in picker.

The worker's framing was slightly off, which I caught by inspecting the artifacts directly. The truth:

FF was decided 6a (mirror push of full history) back on 2026-05-28 because rounds 1+2 audited history clean. The strict SOP config caught what those audits missed. Pushing full history exposes `22b12844`'s blob to the public.

## The mail-password rotation question (deploy-track adjacent)

That commit's message says APP_KEY was rotated + sessions invalidated. **It says nothing about the leaked mail password.** If never rotated, that's also a deploy-track incident — `MAIL_PASSWORD_ENCRYPTED` may still authenticate against the prod SMTP today.
